clue.text: Lead deserters head north

indicators.note: in a down light, heading north means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rats are proverbially the first to desert a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A commander sends men who have run away back up the road northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead role in a film or play is the starring role, so the lead performer is its headline name.

clue.text: Use this when in the Sahara, bickering

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words Sahara and bickering, running across the comma

explanation.surface: Advice for travellers who fall out with each other in the desert: argue in the local tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is extended: 'Use this when in the Sahara' points to the region's language, with 'in' doing double duty as the hidden-word signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of North Africa and the Sahara's peoples is the tongue a traveller there would speak.

clue.text: Men partial to get drunk in this house

indicators.note: drunk men stagger about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A dig at legislators: the men here like getting drunk on the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Commons and House of Lords are the chambers of the British legislature, each called a house.

clue.text: Father grabbed the girl and ran

indicators.note: the word for father holds the girl between its letters, as if grabbing her

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A parent seizes his daughter and runs off.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to run quickly, so the past tense matches ran.

clue.text: See 6
Piano's working for new arrival

parts.note: the small grand piano made for living rooms is named for an infant, and the possessive keeps its S
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is in use to welcome a newborn.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Piano's' is kept, so the piano word ends in S before ON; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn grandchild is a new arrival in the family.

clue.text: Sort of crane to install ring in annex

indicators.note: to install the ring in the annex is to fit it inside the word for annex

parts.note: a wing is an extension added to a building, an annex
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: Builders use a crane to fit a ring into an extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of crane' looks like building machinery; it is the bird, the rare North American crane.
explanation.definitionFit: The whooping crane is a species of tall North American bird, so the word names one sort.

clue.text: Spot in the Hautes-Pyrénées

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the hyphenated French place name, across the hyphen

explanation.surface: Seeing something in a mountainous French department.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, a synonym of the literary verb.

clue.text: Flinch from Arthur, in a fix

indicators.note: being in a fix means being in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a man named Arthur who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word, and 'in a' joins Arthur as fodder, though it reads as part of 'in a fix'.
explanation.definitionFit: Not turning a hair is the idiom for not flinching, so the phrase means show alarm or flinch.

clue.text: With a hostess improperly chasing the above tennis player, the end is inevitable

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the anagram follows the tennis player's surname

parts.note: the Arthur of the clue above is Arthur Ashe, the American Wimbledon champion

indicators.note: doing something improperly means doing it wrongly, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: these words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hostess behaving badly in pursuit of a tennis star is doomed to a bad end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' puts the anagram STOASHES after the tennis player. The phrase from the funeral service is also a Bowie song title.
explanation.definitionFit: The burial service phrase reminds mourners that death is certain, so it expresses that the end is inevitable.

clue.text: Rise of Hilaire Belloc

indicators.note: the letters are part of the writer's full name, straddling first name and surname

explanation.surface: The rise to fame of the Anglo-French writer Hilaire Belloc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' looks like a noun about a career; it is a verb, to rise up against authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise up against rulers is to revolt, so the verb sense matches.

clue.text: Fine and nice-looking fish

parts.note: hunky means attractive, said of a well-built man
the dory, or John Dory, is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Praise for a handsome fish on the slab.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase means everything is fine and going well; also the title of a Bowie album.

clue.text: Peter with an amusing kind of music

parts.note: the name Peter comes from the Greek for stone
droll means amusing in a dry way

explanation.surface: A man named Peter and a witty sort of musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; 'an' is taken as written, and its N joins the D of the word for amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: The genre born in 1950s America from blues and country is a kind of popular music.

clue.text: Be revolting and look revoltingly up and over top of bra

indicators.note: the reversed look sits over, that is around, the first letter of bra
revolting means turning back, and up in a down light means the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: to leer is to look lecherously

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone leers disgustingly at a woman's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revoltingly' looks like disgust at the leering; it signals the turnaround. Rebel Rebel is a Bowie song, hence two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to revolt against authority, so being revolting in that sense is the verb.

clue.text: Knowing no bounds, Medicis push back for the ultimate escape

indicators.note: back means the trimmed letters are then read in reverse order
a word that knows no bounds has lost its outer letters, so each word is trimmed at both ends

explanation.surface: The limitless ambition of the Medici family forces a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knowing no bounds' reads as describing Medici ambition, but it trims both words at each end; 'back' then turns the joined remains around.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking one's own life is a grim, final way out, which the clue calls the ultimate escape.

clue.text: Sporadically gets darker, rising within a short distance

indicators.note: the reversed word sits within the word for a short distance

parts.note: inches are a short distance, as in missing by inches

indicators.note: rising in a down light means the word is read upwards, from the end

parts.note: tans means gets darker in the sun

explanation.surface: The sky darkens now and then as night comes on by degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in bits and pieces, with gaps between, is doing it sporadically.

clue.text: Pitchers titchers?

parts.note: titchers is stitchers with the first letter gone, so the clue asks for another word for stitchers, people who sew, with its first letter gone too

explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: 'titchers' is stitchers less its S, so take a word for stitchers, SEWERS, less its S as well; what is left also means pitchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Jugs with wide mouths for pouring water are pitchers, especially the old washstand kind.

clue.text: Knife that's commemorated here

definitions.meaning: the large sheath knife named after the American frontiersman Jim ...
the singer whose death this anniversary puzzle marks, honoured across the grid

explanation.definitionFit: One surname belongs both to a frontier knife and to the singer this tribute puzzle celebrates.

clue.text: Thought to have secured victory right in the middle of the action

parts.note: won means secured victory

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the centre of the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action

explanation.surface: A competitor believes the battle was won while still in the thick of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wondered and thought are both past tenses for turning something over in the mind.

clue.text: Island or not?

parts.note: the Isle of the same name lies in the Irish Sea, yet John Donne wrote that no such person is an island

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings meet: the island between Britain and Ireland, and Donne's line 'No man is an island', which says the word is not an island at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an island in the Irish Sea and a human being, which Donne said is never an island.

clue.text: The Guardian finally kick the bucket: editor held in compiler's arms

indicators.note: the newspaper and the final letters are held inside the word for compiler's

parts.note: a compiler talking of himself would say my
the newspaper speaking of itself says us

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: The setter fears his newspaper is dying while an editor is clutched in his arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Musketry is the use of muskets, the infantry's arms, so the word stands for small arms or gunfire.

clue.text: House guest in transit the other way round

indicators.note: read the other way round, the clue says in house guest, so the letters lie inside those two words

explanation.surface: A guest in someone's home is travelling in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way round' tells the solver to read the clue back to front: 'in house guest', with the definition 'transit' then at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth move from one piece of music or topic to the next is a transition, the sense of transit here.

clue.text: Lunatics lacking a form of medication

indicators.note: a form of a word is a version of it reshaped, and lacking says the letter a drops out of the pool first

explanation.surface: Psychiatric patients without a particular kind of drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a soothing syrupy cough medicine, a form of medication.

clue.text: See 10
Tasty piece of nipple?

parts.note: a slang word for a nipple followed by a word for a small piece gives a word for a dainty morsel

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer is a small part of a teat; whole, it is a delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty morsel of food, or a juicy snippet of gossip.

clue.text: Champions need a higher oestrogen dose

indicators.note: a dose is a measured portion, so a portion of these two words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Top athletes are said to need more of a female hormone.
explanation.definitionFit: Champions and heroes are both people admired for great deeds; also a Bowie song title.

clue.text: Most fair, if minister adopts the riot act at last

indicators.note: the minister takes those letters in, as if adopting them

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the three preceding words

explanation.surface: A clergyman reads out the law against disorder at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of beautiful, so the most beautiful is the superlative of pretty.

clue.text: "To knit or not knit" sounds like some wisdom

indicators.note: sounds like means the word is heard and spelt differently

parts.note: a pearl of wisdom is a wise saying

explanation.surface: A knitting dilemma phrased like Hamlet's soliloquy, offered as a wise saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on Hamlet's 'To be or not to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: The purl stitch is the reverse of the plain knit stitch, so it is knitting, yet not a knit.

clue.text: Prison term for the enemy

definitions.meaning: doing a stretch inside is serving this
the passing years are called the enemy, as in the saying that it is the enemy of all

explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner does it as a sentence, and it is the foe that ages everyone.

clue.text: End of life wasted in calling for nurse

indicators.note: wasted means lost, so that letter is taken out of the word for calling

parts.note: a calling is a vocation or career

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A vocation squandered at the close of a lifetime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks after a sick or elderly person is a carer, as a nurse does.

clue.text: See 13 across
Note hesitation about hospital discharge

indicators.note: the note and hesitation go about, around, the hospital letter

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A patient pauses over going home from the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The H goes inside RE, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Shell uncovered in Israel exploded to cause a disturbance

indicators.note: the trimmed shell goes in among the jumbled letters
exploded means the letters of the country are blown apart and reassembled
uncovered means the outer letters of the word are stripped away

explanation.surface: An exposed shell detonates in the Middle East, causing an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' turns Israel into RAISEL, and the uncovered shell HEL goes in before its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise hell is the idiom for kicking up a fuss or causing a disturbance.
